drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna need to teach that one who ate redeemed second tithe or redeemed consecrated food may be included in a zimmun?
outcomeNote: The redundancy objection is answered by narrowing the mishna to a redemption in which the fifth was not added.

segments.he: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ: פְּשִׁיטָא! הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּתַן אֶת הַקֶּרֶן, וְלֹא נָתַן אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ. וְהָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאֵין חוֹמֶשׁ מְעַכֵּב.
segments.en: The mishna states that if, among the diners, one ate «second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed,» he may be included in a zimmun.The Gemara remarks: «It is obvious» that if these items were redeemed that one could participate in a zimmun. The Gemara responds: «With what are we dealing here?» We are dealing with «a case» where the consecrated property was not completely redeemed, i.e., «where one gave» payment for «the principal,» the value of the tithe, «but he did not give» payment for «the fifth» that he must add when redeeming items that he consecrated; «and» the mishna «teaches us» that failure to add «the fifth does not invalidate» the redemption.
